column1: #Text=chore: update to mermaid v12 and derive the diagram theme from its defaults

#Text=Updates mermaid to **v12** together with the companion `@mermaid-js/*` packages, drops the now-redundant `@mermaid-js/layout-elk`, and replaces the editor's hard-coded `"theme": "default"` with a theme that follows each diagram type's own mermaid default (and its dark variant when the site is dark).

#Text=- **`@mermaid-js/layout-elk` removed.** Mermaid 12 bundles ELK and registers it automatically (it is also the new default layout). Keeping the package would ship a second copy of the layout engine and its `1.0.0` release still declares a `mermaid@^11` peer range. `src/lib/util/mermaid.ts` now only registers tidy-tree, which is not bundled.

#Text=- **Peer-dependency warnings.** `@mermaid-js/layout-tidy-tree@1.0.0` and `@mermaid-js/mermaid-zenuml@1.0.0` still declare `mermaid@^11` as a peer. pnpm reports this as a warning only; the upstream packages need their peer ranges bumped.
#Text=- The app does not use the removed `defaultRenderer` option or the removed layout-internal exports, and `standardizeDiagramType` already normalises the diagram ids that changed.

#Text=Mermaid 12 gives ten config sections their own default theme (`redux-color` with the `neo` look for flowchart, swimlane, agentflow, sequence, class, state, ER, requirement, use case and Venn); everything else uses the global `default`. Pinning `"theme": "default"` in every config, as the editor used to, opted every user out of that.

#Text=- **`syncManagedTheme` (state module).** After every validation, and whenever the site switches light/dark, the theme is set to the current diagram type's default — `getDefaultTheme(diagramType)` reads the config section's `theme` from `mermaid.mermaidAPI.defaultConfig`, falling back to the global one — or, in dark mode, `darkVariantOf` it: redux themes get their `-dark` variant (`redux-color` → `redux-dark-color`), anything else becomes `dark`. It converges after one update because the next validation finds the theme already in place.

#Text=- **Only editor-set themes are replaced.** `isManagedTheme` accepts a missing theme, the global default, every section default and their dark variants. A theme the user typed into the config (`forest`, `neo`, `base`, …) is never touched, in either mode or when the diagram type changes.
